title: Pre-washing needlework fabric
subtitle: Why linen needs washing before stitching and how to do it without distorting the weave.
excerpt: Linen and some cottons shrink by 2 to 5% on their first wash. Pre-washing before stitching prevents the finished piece from puckering or distorting when it is eventually cleaned.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Preparation of fabric before needlework.
Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746. Fabric preparation notes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiffening agent applied to woven fabric at the mill to keep threads aligned during manufacture. Sizing washes out the first time the fabric is laundered, which often causes slight shrinkage.

content.text: Linen and some cotton fabrics contain

and may shrink on their first wash. A finished needlework piece washed for the first time without pre-treatment can pucker significantly, particularly around densely stitched areas. Pre-washing takes ten minutes and removes this risk.
All linen evenweave and embroidery linen: always pre-wash. Linen shrinks 2 to 5% on its first wash.
Cotton evenweave: pre-wash if you intend to wash the finished piece.
Aida cloth: optional. Most cotton Aida has minimal sizing and low shrinkage. Pre-wash if the project is decorative and will be washed.
Prepare the fabric edges before washing: overcast or fold the edges to prevent fraying in the water.
Soak in cool water for 15 to 20 minutes. Do not use soap on the first pre-wash.
Roll the fabric in a clean dry towel and press gently to remove excess water. Do not wring.
Press the damp fabric on the wrong side with a warm iron, keeping the grain straight. Stretch gently back to square if needed.
Allow to dry flat or roll on a clean tube. Do not fold through the design area.

items.symptom: The fabric comes out of the wash noticeably smaller
items.cause: Sizing washed out and fibres contracted. This is normal for linen.
items.fix: This is what pre-washing is supposed to do. Press while damp to restore the correct size before cutting and marking for the project.

items.symptom: The grain is skewed after washing
items.cause: The fabric was wrung out or dried hanging unevenly.
items.fix: While damp, pull the cloth gently on the diagonal in both directions to square the grain, then press flat. If the grain doesn't correct, soak again and press more firmly while damp.

content.text: Pre-washing is particularly important for any piece intended for daily use or display near a window where it will be washed regularly.
also removes any faint colour from the dye bath, which can sometimes transfer to pale thread in washing.
